title: SwitchBot enters the AI wearable game with a bold new bet
excerpt: Can it succeed where others have failed?
content_html:
Published Sep 3, 2026, 10:05 AM EDT

Timi is the news and deals reporter for Android Police, who has been reporting on technology since 2008. He has worked in tech retail and also the IT space, providing hardware and software support, which gives him a unique perspective on the tech that he covers. This allows him to effectively break down complex subjects into easy-to-read pieces that even casual readers can enjoy. Before joining Android Police, he was a news writer for XDA, where he eventually transitioned to covering deals. He also worked as an editor and reporter for Neowin, where he covered news and attended major tech events like CES. He also reviewed phones, tablets, PC products, and other devices. In addition, he also created video content for the Neowin YouTube channel.

A ton of AI-focused gadgets have hit the market over the past few years, but we haven't really seen one break out and become truly successful. Several factors are at play, but that won't stop brands from continuously trying. It looks like SwitchBot is ready to give it a try, introducing the AI MindClip at IFA 2026 in Berlin.

This one could have some legs

SwitchBot is well established in smart home products, offering a range of devices like smart locks, smart shades, robot vacuums, security cameras, smart trackers, and more. So, while the AI MindClip is a little outside what it usually offers, we think that the brand is well suited to pulling it off.

With a device like this, support matters most. When you're buying something new, you want to know the company behind it will be around for a while. The AI MindClip is a "lightweight clip-on wearable AI assistant" that can turn your daily conversations into powerful personal notes.

The device weighs just 68 grams and can record up to 20 hours with 64GB of internal storage. It also supports speaker separation, allowing it to distinguish who's talking and split the content into manageable chunks when multiple speakers are involved.

The important part of this, and any AI tool, is the ability to search and organize the content captured. You can do this using the SwitchBot app or the brand's website. SwitchBot says the AI MindClip can organize content by arranging "captured moments are arranged into Timeline, Priority, Daily Memory, Weekly Summary, and To-Do Overview."

For better integration, the device can sync with Google Calendar, Apple Calendar, and Reminders. Naturally, privacy is always a concern, and SwitchBot says the AI MindClip offers "encrypted pairing and file transfer, end-to-end encryption, and in-app privacy and data management settings."

The best part is that the AI MindClip won't cost all that much, with an MSRP of $119.99. However, you may require a subscription service plan if you record more than 300 minutes each month. SwitchBot offers a six-month free trial of the Pro plan, which includes 1,200 minutes of use.

Users can sign up for the Pro plan in one, six, and 12-month increments. A month of service costs $15.99; six months cost $59.99; and 12 months cost $99.99. There's also an Unlimited plan for $239.99 for 12 months.
